replication.target_description: Desirability predictor of item-level self-minus-other trait ratings, controlling for controllability and their interaction; Table 6 (printed p. 1014, article p. 10) identifies the final regression result, with matching coefficient in Table 5.

n.sample_role: Trait items: analytic observations are trait-level means, not contributing participants.
n.exclusions: All 149 traits used. Main-report participant data omit six non-US respondents (four first-wave and two second-wave); further participant-exclusion sensitivity analyses are separately reported in the supplement. No trait-item exclusions are stated for this model.
n.location: pp. 1007–1008, Design and Analyses / Traits; p. 1013 Table 5
n.quote: Analyses were conducted on an item ... level by averaging all participant ratings on each dimension for ... each trait. ... A total of 149 traits were used in the present study.

p.location: p. 1013, Table 5, final-model Desirability row and significance footnote; p. 1014 Table 6 matching B = .45

notes: Identity independently confirmed from primary article header: Replication and Extension of Alicke (1985) Better-Than-Average Effect for Desirable and Controllable Traits; Ignazio Ziano, Pui Yan (Cora) Mok, Gilad Feldman; DOI 10.1177/1948550620948973. Published 2021 volume 12(6), copyright 2020; supplied reference is the same work. Canonical text contains the published article and supplementary material, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied. Target selected by desirability/self-minus-other outcome and article p. 10/Table 6, not numeric matching or input order. Table 6 reports final-model unstandardized B .45 [.39, .51]; Table 5 reports the matching .45***, where *** means p < .001. Earlier additive model .46*** is distinct; interaction .19*** and correlation .77 are distinct tests. These are not substituted for the target. The n=149 comes from the explicit trait count plus explicit item-level averaging analysis, not regression degrees of freedom or a participant sum. Participant recruitment counts 670 and 903 are contributor counts, not analytic N.
